text: Contractor/Businessman

My name is Ernie Glasgow, and I am running for Orange City Council, District 1. I have proudly called Orange home for nearly 58 years. My wife and I, who have been married for 42 years, are both graduates of Orange High School. Over the decades, I have watched our city grow and change, and I believe those changes have made Orange a better place to live. My commitment to our community is reflected in my years of public service. I served on the OUSD Facilities Advisory Committee (2003-2004), the YMCA Board (2004-2010), the City Traffic Committee (2012-2015), and the Planning Commission (2015-2023). I also serve as a board member of the Union Roofers Contractor Association and as Co-Chairman of the Union Roofers Trust. My goal is to preserve the small-town character that makes Orange unique while responsibly planning for growth. Old Towne is the heart of our community, but our surrounding neighborhoods deserve the same care and protection. We must also protect our neighborhoods from corporations and LLCs purchasing single-family homes and converting them into high-density housing compounds. With my experience, dedication, and proven record of service, I respectfully ask for your vote.

text: Real Estate Agent

I'm AJ Ricci, born at St. Joseph Hospital, raised in Orange. My entire education has been built in this city, from OUSD through Santiago Canyon College to Chapman University, where I’ve earned my degree in Political Science and ongoing education in real estate. Orange is my home, and I've spent my life promoting it.

I’ve served in public safety at a neighboring police department, and today I volunteer with the Community Emergency Response Team administered through the Orange Fire Department. In my professional career I’ve introduced countless families to calling Orange their home and have helped local businesses open their doors right here in Orange. I know what it takes to keep Orange’s economy moving forward.

I’ve seen Orange’s challenges firsthand through my years living in this city. We need to build a more efficient city hall and not settle for shortsighted policies that only fix today’s problems for a few years. I’m committed to solutions built to serve Orange for the next twenty years and beyond.
Orange needs Transparency, Efficiency, and Accountability.
I respectfully ask for your vote.

text: Business Owner
My life is rooted in Orange. My husband and I are raising our children here. I own a small business in Old Towne Orange. I know what families and local businesses are up against, I live it every day.

As Chair of the City of Orange Park Planning and Community Events Commission, and a graduate of Leadership Orange and Citizens Police Academy, I’ve seen what City Hall does well and where residents deserve better. When Treats in the Streets needed help, I went to work, helping raise over $40,000 to save it and $10,000 for the Orange City Firefighters Foundation. I’ve received the Woman of Impact and Woman of the Year awards for my commitment and service in our community.
As your City Councilmember, I’ll:
Keep Orange safe by supporting our police, firefighters, and emergency responders.
Bring fiscal responsibility back to City Hall by protecting essential services while addressing Orange’s budget challenges.
Protect Old Towne Orange’s historic character and help small businesses thrive.
Put Orange residents first by increasing transparency, accountability and responsiveness in city government.
I’m honored to be endorsed by the Orange City Firefighters Association, Mayor Dan Slater, and Councilwoman Arianna Barrios.
There’s no place like Orange: I will fight to preserve our quality of life. I respectfully ask for your vote.
www.brandyfororange.com

text: General Manager

I'm running for city council because Orange is my home — I'm raising two kids in our public schools, and my wife owns a small business here. I've seen firsthand what it takes for a family and a business to thrive in this city, and I want to bring that perspective to City Hall.

My priorities are straightforward: make Orange a place where businesses want to open, grow, and hire, so we have good jobs and a strong tax base without overburdening residents. I'll work to cut red tape for local entrepreneurs, support smart development that fits our neighborhoods, and make sure growth actually benefits the people who already live here.

Child safety is personal to me. I'll push for safe routes to school, well-lit and secure parks, and real coordination between families, schools, first responders, and local businesses — because a safe community is the foundation everything else is built on.
I'm not interested in partisan fights. I'm interested in practical results: a city that works for families, welcomes business, and moves forward.
